authoredNote: PERL-ONTOLOGY. The two `qw(...)` arrays are one `quoted_word_list` node each, so BOTH names on a line claim that line and neither claims the next — that is the rule the lane already applies to `extends` (PERL-MR12) and it is what `lineOfNameWithin` exists for. The `%EXPORT_TAGS` row is the one shape where the fat-comma KEY is the export: `all` and `some` are the tag names a caller passes to `import`, and the backslash-reference and the arrayref beside them are payload and are NOT exported names. Line numbers are read off the numbered source, which carries a six-line header comment.
rationale: The `exports` LABEL did not exist for perl; the lane had 2,170 export NAMES as `ExportInfo` payload and zero edges, so a module's exported API was in the store and in no graph — and `bb_graph --mode usages` reads `relationship_type IN ('imports','exports')`. All three Exporter surfaces are here in one file so they cannot be fixed one at a time. The `exports` EDGE is 0.9 and not 1.0 because the array only TAKES EFFECT when `Exporter` is reachable from this package's `@ISA` — a fact this file does not always write — so the reason code says so rather than the edge pretending otherwise. Note `use Exporter 'import'` on line 5 makes it effective HERE, and that is the control beside the pinned rows: the analyzer does not need to see it to be right, and must not claim it resolved it. NOTE ON THE SOURCE: the subs are at FILE SCOPE, not in a `package`, and that is deliberate. A perl `sub` inside a package becomes a `method` owned by it, and the harness's export invariant resolves an export against top-level symbols only — so a package-scoped Exporter fixture would be asserting a harness rule rather than an analyzer rule. The real shape is exercised by `imports-and-exports.pm`; this file isolates the three Exporter SURFACES and the edge they produce.

expectRelationships.note: tier: the source states this edge: a declaration or a written name, confidence >= 0.9
BOTH words of one `qw(...)` node claim the line the node is on. Reading only the first would lose half of every Exporter array in a corpus.
the OPTIONAL half. Reading only `@EXPORT` lost it: exports across seven corpora went from 795 to 2,170.
a `%EXPORT_TAGS` KEY is an exported TAG name, and it is the fat-comma key rather than the payload

forbidRelationships.note: the payload of a tag is a backslash-reference to an array, not an exported name
`[qw(epsilon)]` is a tag's PAYLOAD — the names it pulls in, which the module exports only when that tag is requested. Reading it here would claim an unconditional export.
